title: Investigation and characterization of neurobiological and neurophysiological features of migraine patients, before and after a neurofeedback intervention on trigger avoidance behavior.
summary: The aim of this study is (part A) to better understand the development and biological processes of migraine and (part B) to investigate whether EEG neurofeedback training can help to reduce sensitivity to migraine-specific triggers.

interventions.name:
Neurofeedback case group: Patients with migraine diagnosed according to ICHD-3 criteria. 

Collection of questionnaires, neurobiological characterisation, examination of brain activity using EEG and EEG-neurofeedback training.

Control group: test subjects without migraine or headache disorders. 

Questionnaires, neurobiological characterisation, examination of brain activity using EEG.

Sham case group: Patients with migraine diagnosed according to ICHD-3 criteria. 

Collection of questionnaires, neurobiological characterisation, examination of brain activity using EEG and Sham-neurofeedback training.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients with migraine diagnosed according to ICHD-3 criteria
- Test subjects without migraine or headache disorders for the control group
Exclusion criteria:
- Inability to understand the study instructions
- Hearing and visual impairment
- Epilepsy
- Taking psychostimulants or other medications that could affect the study results
could influence the study results
- Current pregnancy
- High blood pressure
